no check-in follows a report that was not delivered; a check-in after it would tell the receiver all is well while a failure is untold (SPEC-396 R7, A7)

only a static alert template reads as whole; with another state also read as whole, a template in that state is never reported (SPEC-396 R5, A5)
an invocation id that is not 32 hexadecimal digits makes the read unreadable; keyed instead, the check-in follows an answer the route cannot trust (SPEC-396 R5, A5)

the first run of an episode exits 1, so OnFailure= pages through the alert sender; exiting 0, the route's own failure pages nobody (SPEC-396 R9, A7)

a run that delivers every request it makes ends the episode, so the next failure pages again; with the episode kept open, a later outage is never paged (SPEC-396 R9, A7)
the record holds the keys of this read only, so a key whose instance is gone is dropped; kept, a path whole again still holds every key once reported (SPEC-396 R6, A6)
